question: What is the primary purpose of standard precautions in healthcare delivery?

options.A: To replace transmission-based precautions in under-resourced clinical settings
options.B: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene when wearing sterile surgical gloves
options.C: To isolate patients who have been confirmed to carry multi-drug resistant organisms
options.D: To reduce the risk of transmission of pathogens from both recognized and unrecognized sources

explanation: Standard precautions are applied universally to all patients regardless of infection status because many carriers are asymptomatic or undiagnosed. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which body fluid is explicitly excluded from the universal application of standard precautions?
explanation: Unless sweat contains visible blood, it is the only body secretion excluded from standard precautions because it generally does not transmit bloodborne or contact pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary target of standard precautions within the chain of infection?
explanation: Barriers, hand hygiene, and environmental cleaning act primarily by interrupting how pathogens travel between the source and the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: An infectious agent leaves the patient through a specific body opening. What is this link in the chain called?
explanation: The path by which a pathogen leaves its host is termed the portal of exit, which includes respiratory tracts, broken skin, and body fluids. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: When is the use of soap and water specifically preferred over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: After every single interaction with an uninfected patient
options.D: When entering a general medical ward in the morning

explanation: Physical dirt and organic matter can shield microorganisms, rendering alcohol rubs less effective and necessitating physical removal with soap and water. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical difference between transient and resident skin flora?

options.A: Resident flora cause immediate systemic infections, while transient flora are completely harmless
options.B: Transient flora form spores that resist alcohol, while resident flora are easily killed by plain soap
options.C: Resident flora are acquired solely from hospital environments, while transient flora are naturally occurring
options.D: Transient flora are easily removed by routine hand hygiene, whereas resident flora dwell deeper in skin layers

explanation: Transient microorganisms are picked up during daily activities and reside on the superficial skin layers, making them easy to wash away. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to irrigate a large, contaminated wound with normal saline, expecting splashing. Which PPE combination is most appropriate?

options.A: Plastic apron and sterile surgical boots
options.B: Gloves, fluid-resistant gown, mask, and face shield
options.C: Sterile gloves and an N95 respirator mask only
options.D: Clean gloves and a standard surgical cap

explanation: Wound irrigation generates splashes and sprays that threaten the hands, clothing, face, and mucous membranes, requiring comprehensive barrier protection. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is a primary nursing action to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries after administering an injection?

options.A: Place the used syringe on a tray and carry it to the utility room for dismantling
options.B: Break the needle off the syringe barrel using forceps prior to throwing it away
options.C: Use a one-handed scoop technique to recap the needle securely before disposal
options.D: Dispose of the unsheathed needle immediately into a puncture-resistant container

explanation: Avoiding recapping altogether is the safest approach; needles should go straight into a nearby sharps container. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous to overfill a sharps disposal container in a clinical ward?

options.A: It causes the plastic material to dissolve prematurely due to chemical reactions
options.B: It prevents the locking mechanism from releasing the pleasant scent liners
options.C: It increases the risk of protruding needles injuring staff handling or disposing of the box
options.D: It makes the container too heavy for hospital waste management personnel to lift

explanation: Overfilled containers leave sharp tips exposed at the opening, directly threatening anyone closing or transporting the bin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: What is the recommended alternative if a tissue is unavailable when an individual needs to cough or sneeze?

options.A: Covering the mouth with both bare hands and rubbing them
options.B: Coughing directly into the bend of the inner elbow
options.C: Turning the head downward and coughing into open air
options.D: Placing a hand over the nose and wiping it on a uniform

explanation: Using the inner elbow prevents hands from becoming contaminated with respiratory droplets that would otherwise spread to surfaces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an intended component of respiratory hygiene in a waiting area? (Select one)

options.A: Offering surgical masks to individuals presenting with a cough
options.B: Displaying educational signs illustrating proper cough etiquette
options.C: Providing communal cloth handkerchiefs for patient use
options.D: Placing alcohol-based hand rub dispensers near the entrance

explanation: Communal cloth handkerchiefs would facilitate pathogen transmission rather than prevent it; disposable tissues should always be used. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: How should reusable non-critical patient care equipment, such as a stethoscope or blood pressure cuff, be handled between patients?

options.A: Stored in a shared drawer until the end of the shift
options.B: Rinsed under cold running tap water for five seconds
options.C: Cleaned and disinfected according to facility protocols
options.D: Wiped only if visible blood or body fluid is present

explanation: Reusable equipment can transfer microorganisms between patients and must be cleaned and disinfected after every individual use. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: Which surfaces in a patient care ward typically require the most frequent cleaning and disinfection attention?

options.A: Interior walls behind heavy patient wardrobes
options.B: Floor skirting boards in private examination rooms
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and call buttons
options.D: Ceiling tiles and upper window glass frames

explanation: High-touch surfaces are repeatedly contacted by hands, making them primary vectors for cross-contamination in ward environments. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury on the ward?

options.A: Squeeze the wound vigorously to force out any trapped blood
options.B: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Soak the hand in a basin of pure household bleach solution
options.D: Apply strong iodine tincture and bandage the finger tightly

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water removes surface contaminants and helps reduce infection risk without traumatizing the tissue. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h8)

question: Why is harsh scrubbing or squeezing discouraged following an accidental percutaneous sharps injury?

options.A: It can damage delicate local tissue and increase pathogen absorption
options.B: It neutralizes the effectiveness of subsequent post-exposure prophylaxis
options.C: It causes immediate chemical burns on the surrounding epidermis
options.D: It violates standard hospital administrative documentation policies

explanation: Aggressive manipulation of a puncture wound breaks down local cellular barriers, potentially driving pathogens deeper into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h8)
